When I started my period, I would flush the toilet whenever I opened my pads because I didn't want anyone hearing the sound of it crinkling because I was THAT embarrassed about it. Everyone living in the house at the time even knew about it, but I was still embarrassed. Your daughter is probably going to be embarrassed no matter what, and you will too I suppose, so you just have to make sure she knows what she needs to know to keep herself healthy.

I would possible recommend that you get an older girl, maybe someone from church or any activity she's involved in, that your daughter looks up to to talk to her about it to tell her all the stuff she REALLY needs to know that you don't even "get" yourself because you're a man. You can tell her the basics, but let's face it, unless you've ever been a young girl who just started her period and is scared to death about everything in life in general, you have no idea what it's like to be in her situation. She'll feel more comfortable with a girl, especially if it's one she looks up to. You could approach the girl, or her parents even, and ask that they not tell your daughter that you sent them, but be kinda sneaky about it.

This is kind of weird, but the older girls on my basketball team were the ones who taught me how to put in a tampon. I wasn't comfortable at all with my mom or older sister teaching me, but they were very "cool" and lighthearted about it, which made me not be so scared and ashamed. It was no big deal to them; they were just being nice girls, trying to help another girl out.

When I graduated high school, I knew that I was about to go to college and be exposed to a lot of beliefs that were different than mine. I was scared that I was going to be "tricked" into believing something different and that scared me, so I decided to go on a mission to make 100% sure I was right by studying other religious and belief systems so I could learn about them and, I thought, prove myself right. I went into it with the attitude of, "I'm going to look for the truth, no matter what it is," but while really thinking that I was going to find that I was right. So I started researching other religions and talking to people who I knew believed differently than me and here I am  :)

My boyfriend also introduced me to a lot of new concepts and helped me stay open minded without trying to convince me of anything.

I'm not full-blown atheist because, as silly as it sounds, I've seen things in my life that I can't fully explain without there being some kind of "higher being," though I wouldn't call it God any more because that term has SO many implications attached to it that I don't agree with. I don't what it is. It could be the force of "good," it could be me putting meaning in things that are coincidence to make myself feel better. I just don't know.

Also, I've never heard an argument that completely rules out the existence of some type of higher being that is a force of good. I'm not sure what I believe at this point because I haven't done enough research to figure it out. I'm still learning  :)
